next_state_election.name: Gubernatorial General Election
next_state_election.source_name: Maryland State Board of Elections — 2026 General Election

glance_notes.source_name: Maryland State Board of Elections — 2026 Gubernatorial Election
glance_notes.text: 2026 General Election Registration Deadline: Maryland's advance voter registration deadline for the November 3, 2026 General Election is October 13, 2026. Eligible residents who miss that deadline can still register and vote during early voting or on Election Day by providing proof of residence.

glance_notes.source_name: Maryland State Board of Elections — 2026 General Election
glance_notes.text: Early Voting October 22–29: Early voting for Maryland's 2026 General Election runs from October 22 through October 29, including Saturday and Sunday. Early voting centers are open from 7:00 a.m. until 8:00 p.m. each day, and voters may use any early voting center in their county of residence.

glance_notes.source_name: Maryland State Board of Elections — Mail-in Voting
glance_notes.text: No-Excuse Mail-In Voting: Any registered Maryland voter may vote by mail without providing an excuse. For the 2026 General Election, requests for a ballot delivered by mail or fax are due October 27, while requests for a print-at-home ballot are due October 30.

register.label: Register to Vote
register.content: To register to vote in Maryland, you must be a U.S. citizen, a Maryland resident and at least 16 years old. You cannot vote unless you will be at least 18 years old by the next General Election. A person cannot register if currently serving a sentence of imprisonment for a felony conviction, if convicted of buying or selling votes, or if under guardianship for mental disability and a court has specifically found the person unable to communicate a desire to vote. Eligible residents can register online, by mail or in person through approved registration agencies and local election offices.
register.source_name: Maryland State Board of Elections — Voter Registration
register.internal_note: The Maryland State Board of Elections directly establishes citizenship, Maryland residence, age and disqualification rules. Maryland permits registration beginning at age 16, although a registrant cannot vote unless eligible by age for the applicable election. Maryland's felony rule applies only while the person is currently serving a sentence of imprisonment for a felony conviction; do not incorrectly describe Maryland as requiring completion of probation or parole.

check_registration.label: Check Voter Registration
check_registration.content: Use the Maryland State Board of Elections voter lookup to check your registration record. The service can also provide your polling place and voting districts, display your sample ballot when available, show mail-in and provisional ballot status and allow you to request a duplicate voter registration card.
check_registration.source_name: Maryland State Board of Elections — Voter Lookup
check_registration.internal_note: The State Board's official 2026 General Election page directly identifies the voter lookup as the service for reviewing registration records, sample ballots, polling places, voting districts, mail-in ballot status and provisional ballot status. Supporting official page: [https://elections.maryland.gov/elections/2026/vote2026/](https://elections.maryland.gov/elections/2026/vote2026/).

deadlines.label: Registration Deadlines
deadlines.content: The advance voter registration deadline for Maryland's November 3, 2026 General Election is Tuesday, October 13, 2026. Eligible residents who miss the advance deadline may still register and vote during early voting at an early voting center in their county or on Election Day at the polling place assigned to their residence. Same-day registrants must provide a document proving where they live.
deadlines.source_name: Maryland State Board of Elections — 2026 Gubernatorial Election
deadlines.internal_note: The State Board directly identifies October 13, 2026 as the General Election advance registration deadline. Maryland also allows registration during early voting and on Election Day. Acceptable proof of residence includes an MVA-issued license, permit or ID card, MVA change-of-address card, paycheck, bank statement, utility bill or another government document containing the voter's name and current address.

polling_place.label: Find a Polling Place
polling_place.content: Use Maryland's official voter registration and polling-place lookup to find your assigned Election Day polling location. On Election Day, voters must generally vote at the polling place assigned to their residential address. During early voting, a voter may instead use any early voting center in the county where the voter lives.
polling_place.glance_value: Find your assigned polling place online
polling_place.source_name: Maryland State Board of Elections — Polling Place Lookup
polling_place.internal_note: The official lookup provides both a name search for voter-specific registration and polling-place information and an address search. The State Board's 2026 election guidance confirms that Election Day voters use their assigned polling place while early voters may use any early voting center within their county.

election_day.label: Election Day Voting
election_day.content: Maryland's Gubernatorial General Election is Tuesday, November 3, 2026. Polling places are open from 7:00 a.m. until 8:00 p.m. Voters cast ballots at the polling place assigned to their residence. Maryland also permits eligible residents to register and vote on Election Day by providing acceptable proof of residence. Most registered Maryland voters do not need to show identification before voting, although identification is required in certain circumstances.
election_day.source_name: Maryland State Board of Elections — 2026 General Election
election_day.internal_note: The State Board directly establishes November 3 and 7:00 a.m.-8:00 p.m. voting hours. Same-day registration is explicitly available. Maryland is not a general photo-ID-at-the-polls state; only certain voters are required to provide identification, so avoid describing Maryland as having a universal voter-ID requirement.

polling_hours.label: Polling Hours
polling_hours.content: Maryland polling places are open from 7:00 a.m. until 8:00 p.m. on November 3, 2026. Early voting centers are also open from 7:00 a.m. until 8:00 p.m. on each early voting day from October 22 through October 29.
polling_hours.source_name: Maryland State Board of Elections — Offices and Election Dates
polling_hours.internal_note: The State Board's official 2026 election information directly lists 7:00 a.m.-8:00 p.m. for both General Election early voting and Election Day.

early_voting.label: Early In-Person Voting
early_voting.content: Maryland provides no-excuse early in-person voting. For the November 3, 2026 General Election, early voting runs from Thursday, October 22 through Thursday, October 29, including Saturday and Sunday. Early voting centers are open from 7:00 a.m. until 8:00 p.m. each day. A voter may vote at any early voting center in the county where the voter resides. Eligible residents who are not registered by the advance deadline may also register and vote at an early voting center by providing acceptable proof of residence.
early_voting.source_name: Maryland State Board of Elections — 2026 General Election
early_voting.internal_note: The State Board directly confirms October 22-29, 2026, including the weekend, with 7:00 a.m.-8:00 p.m. daily hours. Maryland allows voters to use any early voting center within their county of residence and provides same-day registration during early voting.

absentee_mail.label: Mail-In Voting
absentee_mail.content: Any registered Maryland voter may vote by mail without providing an excuse. For the November 3, 2026 General Election, a request to receive a ballot by mail or fax must be submitted by October 27. A request for a print-at-home ballot must be submitted by October 30. A voter who misses those deadlines may request a mail-in ballot in person at the local board of elections through 8:00 p.m. on Election Day. A completed ballot returned by mail must be postmarked on or before November 3. Voters may also return completed ballots to an official ballot drop box or other authorized location by the applicable Election Day deadline. Maryland also offers a permanent mail-in ballot list for voters who want ballots automatically sent for future federal and state elections.
absentee_mail.glance_value: No excuse required; mail/fax request by October 27
absentee_mail.source_name: Maryland State Board of Elections — Mail-in Voting
absentee_mail.internal_note: The State Board directly establishes October 27 for ballots delivered by mail or fax and October 30 for print-at-home delivery. The official 2026 election calendar specifies that electronic-delivery requests received by mail are due at 5:00 p.m. October 30, while email/fax requests are due by 11:59 p.m. The calendar also establishes an 8:00 p.m. Election Day deadline for in-person ballot requests. The official General Election page states that mailed ballots must be postmarked on or before November 3. Maryland law requires election agencies to use the term mail-in ballot rather than absentee ballot.

voter_id.label: Voter ID Requirements
voter_id.content: Most registered Maryland voters do not need to show identification before voting. Identification may be required for certain first-time voters whose identifying information was not previously verified, voters whose registration information could not be verified through government records, and voters whose identity is challenged under Maryland law. Eligible residents using same-day registration must provide a document proving residence, such as an MVA-issued license, permit or identification card, a change-of-address card, paycheck, bank statement, utility bill or another government document containing the voter's name and current address.
voter_id.glance_value: Most voters do not need ID
voter_id.source_name: Maryland State Board of Elections — Election Day Questions
voter_id.internal_note: Maryland does not impose a general photo-ID requirement on registered voters. Official State Board election materials state that most registered voters do not need identification. Federal HAVA identification requirements apply to certain first-time voters, and Maryland law also provides procedures when identity is challenged. Same-day registration is separate and requires proof of residence. Do not conflate proof of residence for same-day registration with a universal voter-ID requirement.

accessible_voting.label: Accessible Voting
accessible_voting.content: All Maryland early voting centers are accessible to voters with disabilities, and accessible ballot-marking devices are available at early voting centers and Election Day polling places. These devices support features including audio ballots, keypads, high-contrast displays, enlarged text and compatible assistive equipment. Voters who need assistance may bring someone to help, except an employer or employer's agent, a union officer or agent, or a challenger or watcher. Two election judges may also provide assistance. Maryland also offers an accessible online ballot-marking tool for voters using print-at-home mail-in ballots. The completed ballot must still be printed and returned physically; Maryland does not allow voted ballots to be returned electronically.
accessible_voting.glance_value: Accessible equipment, assistance and ballot-marking tools
accessible_voting.source_name: Maryland State Board of Elections — Accessible Voting
accessible_voting.internal_note: The State Board directly confirms accessible early voting centers, accessible ballot-marking devices at all voting locations, assistance rights and the online accessible ballot-marking system. The ExpressVote system produces a voter-verifiable paper ballot. Maryland expressly prohibits electronic return of voted mail-in ballots.

military_overseas.label: Military & Overseas Voting
military_overseas.content: Maryland provides special registration and mail-in voting procedures for eligible members of the Uniformed Services, Merchant Marine, qualifying spouses and dependents, and U.S. citizens living outside the United States. Covered voters may register online or use the Federal Post Card Application. They may request a mail-in ballot by mail, fax, email or through Maryland's online system, and electronic access to a blank ballot is available. A voter who receives a ballot electronically must still return the completed ballot by mail, authorized drop box or in person; Maryland does not permit voted ballots to be returned by email or fax. Federal law requires Maryland to transmit ballots to qualifying military and overseas voters at least 45 days before the General Election when a timely request has been received.
military_overseas.glance_value: FPCA and electronic ballot delivery available
military_overseas.source_name: Maryland State Board of Elections — Overseas & Military Voters
military_overseas.internal_note: Maryland's UOCAVA registration page directly establishes October 13, 2026 as the advance registration deadline for the General Election. Official absentee guidance confirms FPCA use and ballot requests by mail, fax or email. Maryland's MOVE Act page confirms transmission of federal-only ballots 45 days before the General Election and electronic access when requested. Critically, voted ballots cannot be returned electronically.

student_voting.label: College / Student Voting
student_voting.content: A college student attending school in Maryland may choose to register using a qualifying Maryland school address if the student considers that address to be the student's residence for voting purposes and otherwise meets Maryland's eligibility requirements. A student may instead remain registered at a qualifying home address. A voter may be registered at only one address and may vote only once in an election. Maryland notes that voting residency rules are separate from residency rules used for in-state tuition and advises students receiving residence-dependent financial aid to determine whether changing their voting residence could affect that aid.
student_voting.glance_value: Choose one qualifying home or school voting residence
student_voting.source_name: Maryland State Board of Elections — College Students
student_voting.internal_note: The dedicated State Board student page confirms that a voter may be registered at only one address and vote only once, discusses school-versus-home residence choices, and distinguishes voting residence from in-state tuition residence. It also explains mail-in voting for students who will be away from their registered Maryland address.

sample_ballot.label: Official Sample Ballot
sample_ballot.content: Maryland voters can view their personalized sample ballot through the State Board of Elections voter lookup when General Election ballots are available. Sample ballots are also distributed to voters before an election. Because ballot contents depend on the voter's residential address and electoral districts, voters should use the official voter lookup to review the ballot that applies to their registration. A sample ballot is for voter information only and cannot be cast as an official ballot.
sample_ballot.glance_value: View your ballot through Maryland's voter lookup
sample_ballot.source_name: Maryland State Board of Elections — 2026 General Election
sample_ballot.internal_note: The State Board's current 2026 General Election page provides a View Sample Ballots function and states that voter lookup can display the voter's sample ballot. The State Board's official Rumor Control page at [https://elections.maryland.gov/press_room/rumor_control.html](https://elections.maryland.gov/press_room/rumor_control.html) specifically warns that sample ballots are not mail-in ballots and cannot be submitted as votes. Reverify after General Election ballot certification.

contact.label: Contact the State Election Authority
contact.content: Maryland State Board of Elections, 151 West Street, Suite 200, Annapolis, MD 21401. Mailing address: P.O. Box 6486, Annapolis, MD 21401-0486. Phone: 410-269-2840. Toll-free: 800-222-8683. Maryland Relay Service: 800-735-2258. Office hours are Monday through Friday from 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. For questions involving an individual registration record, polling place, mail-in ballot or other local election matter, voters may also contact their local board of elections.
contact.source_name: Maryland State Board of Elections — Contact Us
contact.internal_note: The current State Board contact page directly verifies the street address, mailing address, 410-269-2840 phone number, 800-222-8683 toll-free number, 800-735-2258 Maryland Relay Service and 8:00 a.m.-5:00 p.m. weekday office hours. The website masks its general email address in retrieved text, so no email address is inserted into reader-facing content without direct verification. No Markdown hyperlink or mailto syntax is used.

official_resources.label: Official State & Local Resources
official_resources.content: Use the Maryland State Board of Elections website for official statewide information about voter registration, election dates, early voting, Election Day voting, mail-in voting, accessibility and military and overseas voting. The State Board's voter services system provides registration lookup, polling-place information, voting districts, sample ballots and ballot-status information. Local boards of elections administer many voter services and election functions within Maryland's counties and Baltimore City.
